ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Treat the projectile motion as independent horizontal and vertical motions. Since the ball is struck horizontally, its initial vertical velocity is 0. Vertically, the ball falls through h = 0.8 m under g = 10 m/s^2, so h = (1/2)gt^2. Thus 0.8 = 5t^2, giving t^2 = 0.16 and t = 0.4 s. Horizontally, the velocity is constant, so v_x = s/t = 1.2/0.4 = 3 m/s. At impact, the vertical velocity is v_y = gt = 10 × 0.4 = 4 m/s downward. The impact speed is the resultant of perpendicular components: v = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 m/s.

method.method_draft: Treat the motion as independent horizontal uniform motion and vertical free fall. Read the launch as horizontal, so initial vertical velocity is zero. From the vertical displacement h=0.8 m with g=10 m/s^2, solve h = (1/2)gt^2 to get t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(1.6/10)=0.4 s. Use the measured horizontal range s=1.2 m and constant horizontal velocity to compute v_x = s/t = 1.2/0.4 = 3 m/s. At impact, compute vertical velocity v_y = gt = 4 m/s downward, then combine perpendicular components: v = sqrt(v_x^2+v_y^2)=sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 m/s.
